answer: Arrival-Jitter Attestation** Each identity must submit a cipher of its request-origin timestamps to a shared log; the verifier measures inter-arrival delta variance. Organic agents show natural jitter, while a Sybil cluster spun up together produces suspiciously tight timing. Identities whose variance falls below a crystal-clear threshold get rate-limited to one action per epoch. To evade, an attacker must run each fake identity on genuinely independent schedules and infrastructure, paying real compute and wall-clock latency per identity rather than a cheap batch script.
